# Resonate MusiX T1 (Piano & Melodic Edition) ### Next-Generation Text-Conditioned Piano & Symbolic Music Transformer [![Model Size](https://img.shields.io/badge/Parameters-50.41M-2B5797.svg)](#technical-specifications) [![Specialization](https://img.shields.io/badge/Focus-Piano%20%7C%20Harmonic%20Melodies-7B2CBF.svg)](#model-summary) [![Architecture](https://img.shields.io/badge/Architecture-RoPE%20%7C%20SwiGLU%20%7C%20Cross--Attention-107C41.svg)](#architecture-details) [![Precision](https://img.shields.io/badge/Precision-bfloat16%20%7C%20TF32-D83B01.svg)](#technical-specifications) [![Hardware](https://img.shields.io/badge/Compute-NVIDIA%20A100%20SXM4-76B900.svg)](#technical-specifications) [![License](https://img.shields.io/badge/License-MIT-gray.svg)](LICENSE)
--- ## Model Summary **Resonate MusiX T1 (Piano & Melodic Edition)** is a 50.41-million parameter autoregressive decoder transformer specialized in generating expressive piano compositions, intricate keyboard counterpoints, and memorable melodic themes directly from natural language prompts. Trained on a curated corpus of **10,000 multi-voice compositions**, the model demonstrates strong proficiency in acoustic piano voicing, lyrical right-hand melodies, dynamic arpeggiated basslines, and rich harmonic chord progressions. Natural language prompts guide key musical attributes including emotional tone, tempo, playing style, dynamic touch, and compositional complexity via continuous cross-attention conditioning. --- ## Piano & Keyboard Capabilities - **Two-Hand Polyphony:** Independently coordinates lower-register bass chords/arpeggios with expressive upper-register melody lines. - **Dynamic Phrasing:** Supports 16 quantized velocity levels, reflecting nuanced key strike intensity from gentle pianissimo to striking forte. - **Zero-Latency Attack:** Generation starts immediately on beat one without introductory pauses or empty measures. - **Anti-Monotony Guard:** Built-in repetition penalty prevents repetitive note hammering, encouraging flowing scalar runs and harmonic transitions. --- ## Local Inference (CLI) Run generation locally on CPU or CUDA GPU: ### 1. Requirements ```bash pip install torch miditok sentence-transformers symusic ``` ### 2. Files Required Keep these files in the same directory: - `generate.py` - `resonate_musix_t1.pt` - `resonate_tokenizer.json` ### 3. Usage ```bash python generate.py ``` Options: - **Prompt:** Text description of the desired music style, tempo, or mood. - **Count:** Number of tracks to generate (default: 1). - **Mode:** - `1`: Dynamic Melody (balanced phrasing and transitions) - `2`: Strict Harmony (tight chord alignment) - `3`: Wild Solo (complex melodic variations) Output `.mid` files are saved directly in the project directory. --- ## Architecture Details Resonate MusiX T1 replaces conventional GPT-2 building blocks with modern architectural primitives: 1. **Rotary Position Embeddings (RoPE):** Operates on complex inner-product rotation ($\theta = 10000.0$), ensuring relative time and bar structure awareness across variable sequence lengths. 2. **SwiGLU Non-Linearity:** Uses a gated linear unit with Swish activation ($d_{ffn} = 1728$, rounded to multiples of 64), providing superior representation capacity per parameter. 3. **RMSNorm (Root Mean Square Normalization):** Placed pre-attention and pre-FFN with $\epsilon = 10^{-6}$ for numerical stability under mixed-precision regimes. 4. **Text Conditioning via Cross-Attention:** Interleaved cross-attention blocks inject 384-dimensional semantic embeddings from `sentence-transformers/all-MiniLM-L6-v2` directly into every transformer layer. 5. **Anti-Repetition & Anti-Silence Engine:** Built-in penalty ($1.28$) and leading rest suppression eliminate silence and note-spamming loops during generation. --- ## Technical Specifications | Parameter | Value | | :--- | :--- | | **Model Type** | Autoregressive Transformer with Cross-Attention | | **Primary Domain** | Expressive Piano & Melodic Polyphonic Arrangements | | **Total Parameters** | 50,412,800 (50.41M) | | **Checkpoint Size** | 192.4 MB (.pt / Safetensors) | | **Context Window ($N_{ctx}$)** | 1024 tokens (~30-45 seconds of continuous polyphony) | | **Hidden Dimension ($d_{model}$)** | 640 | | **Number of Layers** | 8 | | **Attention Heads** | 8 ($d_{head} = 80$) | | **Intermediate FFN Size** | 1728 (SwiGLU) | | **Text Embedding Dimension** | 384 | | **Tokenization Format** | REMI (Revamped MIDI) | | **Vocabulary Size** | 1,024 tokens | | **Training Precision** | bfloat16 / TensorFloat-32 (TF32) | | **Final Loss** | 0.75 Cross-Entropy | --- ## Piano Prompt Engineering Reference | Style Category | Sample Conditioning Prompt | | :--- | :--- | | **Emotional Ballad** | `emotional slow romantic bell piano melody with warm acoustic chords 80 bpm` | | **Lyrical Classical** | `peaceful classical acoustic piano solo with flowing arpeggios and gentle dynamics` | | **Nostalgic Minor Key** | `melancholic piano theme in minor key with deep bass octaves and delicate melody` | | **Uplifting & Bright** | `bright joyful piano melody with fast upbeat chord changes and energetic rhythm` | | **Cinematic Ambient** | `ambient cinematic piano soundtrack theme with spacious reverberant harmonies` | | **Pop / Neo-Classical** | `modern catchy piano hook melody with rhythmic left hand syncopation` | --- ## Playback & Sound Quality The model outputs standard symbolic MIDI (`.mid`). For high-fidelity acoustic playback, open generated files using virtual piano instruments: - **DAWs / VSTs:** Keyscape, Pianoteq, Native Instruments The Grandeur, Addictive Keys. - **SoundFonts (Free):** FluidR3_GM, Salamander Grand Piano, GeneralUser GS. --- ## Limitations - **Instrument Assignment:** Outputs universal MIDI event streams. Instrument realism depends on the downstream SoundFont or VST instrument loaded in your player. - **Context Boundary:** Coherence remains optimal up to 1024 tokens (~45 seconds of audio). --- ## Citation ```bibtex @misc{resonate_musix_t1_2026, author = {Resonate MusiX Team}, title = {Resonate MusiX T1: Dense Polyphonic Piano & Symbolic Music Transformer}, year = {2026}, publisher = {Hugging Face}, howpublished = {\url{https://huggingface.co}} } ``` --- ## License This project is distributed under the [MIT License](LICENSE).

Website · GitHub · The guide · ☕ Buy me a Coffee Machine

> Ruach Studio is open music generation that runs on your own hardware: the model, the score, the adapters and every take stay yours, and nothing is rented by the token. Open models are now good enough to stand on their own, and what was missing is the studio around them: that is what we build, in the open. Music should be free to make and to share: whoever has no voice, no instrument and no studio still has the right to lay their thoughts and feelings onto sound. > **⚠ Not on free cloud GPUs.** Ruach Studio does not run on Google Colab, Kaggle or any free notebook GPU, so don't spend an evening on it there: it is a whole studio, not a notebook. It builds its C++/CUDA engine on the machine it lives on, keeps a server and a lab of Python services running beside it, and takes about 33 GB of disk (60 GB with the Artist). A free session's card, memory, wiped disk and hours-long limit cannot hold that. It wants your own Linux computer, or a server you rent and keep, with an NVIDIA card: 24 GB for everything, 16 GB with the smaller model copies. Everything [Ruach Studio](https://github.com/igrbible/Ruach_Studio) runs on, in one place and laid out as its own folders: the music model and its decoders, the transcriber, the stems' and the sound upscaler's models, Whisper, the style listener, the studio's own adapters, the LoRA Trainer's base, and the Artist's painters with the adapters their authors let be shared. 163 files, 256 GB. A copy of the studio's own disk, file for file: what lies here is what it paints, sings and trains with, and the studio fetches all of it from here alone. **Nothing here is ours but the conversions and the studio's own adapters.** Every other file is its authors' work, unchanged, under its authors' licence, credited below and line by line in `MANIFEST.tsv`. Not affiliated with M-A-P, Comfy Org, Mothersuperior, HaileyStorm, atomtanstudio, storagejuju, OpenAI, Systran, Meta, the Qwen team, Unsloth, lightx2v, Falconsai, prithivMLmods, Civitai or the authors named below. If you are an author and want a file of yours taken down, open a discussion here and it goes. ## Take what you need The studio's own install (`./fetch-models.sh`) takes what your card can run, at a pinned revision, checking each file. By hand, from the studio's root: ```bash hf download goldhub/Ruach_Studio_Models_v2 --local-dir . --include "models/YuE2-3B-Q8_0.gguf" "models/YuE2-Vae-F32.gguf" "models/SheetSage2-Q8_0.gguf" "models/MERT-v2-FullSong-Q8_0.gguf" # to sing: 5.3 GB hf download goldhub/Ruach_Studio_Models_v2 --local-dir . --include "models/YuE2-Vae-*" # the other decoders hf download goldhub/Ruach_Studio_Models_v2 --local-dir . --include "whisper/*" "separation/*" "universr/*" # Whisper, stems, the sound's upscaler hf download goldhub/Ruach_Studio_Models_v2 --local-dir . --include "artwork/Qwen-Image-2512/gguf/*Q4_K_M*" "artwork/Qwen-Image-2512/lightning/*" "artwork/Qwen-Image-2512/*.json" "artwork/Qwen-Image-2512/scheduler/*" "artwork/Qwen-Image-2512/tokenizer/*" "artwork/Qwen-Image-2512/text_encoder/*" "artwork/Qwen-Image-2512/vae/*" "artwork/Qwen-Image-2512/transformer/*" # the Artist on 16 GB hf download goldhub/Ruach_Studio_Models_v2 --local-dir . --include "checkpoints/comfy/checkpoints/yue2_3b_bf16.safetensors" "checkpoints/MERT-v2-FullSong/*" "checkpoints/yue2-mothersuperior-realaudio-tokenizer-v4/*" # the LoRA Trainer's base: 10.5 GB ``` ## Known by its content, not its name `SHA256SUMS` holds each file's SHA-256 (as `sha256sum -c SHA256SUMS` reads it, and as Hugging Face knows the file). `MANIFEST.tsv` adds, for each `.safetensors`, the SHA-256 of its tensors alone (their names and data, its header's metadata aside), with each file's origin and licence. A file renamed after download, or an adapter whose header was rewritten, is the same file or the same adapter all the same: the studio looks for what it needs by these sums, not by the name it was published under. ## What is here | folder | size | what for | from | licence | |---|---|---|---|---| | `models/` | 22.1 GB | **YuE2-3B** (BF16, Q8_0, Q6_K, Q5_K_M), its decoders (**Standard**, **Legacy**, the 0.666 **Blend**) and the score's transcriber: **SheetSage2**'s head with **MERT-v2-FullSong** beside it (F32, Q8_0 each), and Mothersuperior's realaudio **tokenizer** head (F32, Q8_0) | [m-a-p/YuE2-3B](https://huggingface.co/m-a-p/YuE2-3B) and its siblings as GGUF ([Serveurperso/YuE2-GGUF](https://huggingface.co/Serveurperso/YuE2-GGUF)); # StaleyNET checkpoints

[![Source on GitHub](https://img.shields.io/badge/source-GitHub-1D1B20?logo=github)](https://github.com/arpanpathak/staleynet) [![staleynet-audio on crates.io](https://img.shields.io/crates/v/staleynet-audio?label=staleynet-audio)](https://crates.io/crates/staleynet-audio) [![Paper](https://img.shields.io/badge/paper-PDF-6750A4)](https://github.com/arpanpathak/staleynet/blob/main/paper/preprint.pdf) [![Book](https://img.shields.io/badge/book-mdBook-6750A4)](https://github.com/arpanpathak/staleynet/tree/main/book/src) [![Release v0.1.2](https://img.shields.io/github/v/release/arpanpathak/staleynet)](https://github.com/arpanpathak/staleynet/releases) [![Dataset: 3.1 GB](https://img.shields.io/badge/dataset-3.1%20GB-FFD21E?logo=huggingface&logoColor=black)](https://huggingface.co/datasets/arpanpathak/staleynet-data)

Weights for **StaleyNET**, a text-prompted music generator trained from random initialization in Rust on NVIDIA edge GPUs. The Transformer, residual vector quantizer, Griffin-Lim vocoder, and GPU kernels are implemented in the project.

The code, paper, and book live in the companion repository:
<https://github.com/arpanpathak/staleynet>.

## Release v0.1.2

- GitHub release: <https://github.com/arpanpathak/staleynet/releases/tag/v0.1.2>
- `staleynet-audio` 0.1.2 on crates.io: <https://crates.io/crates/staleynet-audio>. Its page explains each audio step with intuition and runnable examples.
- Since v0.1.1: the GPU kernels are organised into one module per topic, the AGX Thor builds against cuda-oxide's main branch, and the paper has been revised with hardware, benchmark and tokenizer appendices.
- New in these repositories: the `lyrics-thor`, `lyrics-thor-long` and `pq-large` runs, and the band-group token caches they train on.
- CI: rustfmt, clippy with warnings denied, cargo-deny, the audio coverage gate, and documentation tests for every example on the crate page.

## At a glance

| Item | Value |
|---|---|
| Checkpointed runs | 9 |
| Parameters | 7,099,904 for text-only runs; 7,165,440 for the lyrics runs; 42,858,496 for `pq-large` |
| Transformer | width 256, 8 heads, 6 layers, context 768 (`pq-large`: width 512, 8 layers, context 1152) |
| Audio tokens | 4 residual codebooks of 1024 entries (`pq-large`: 4 band groups × 4 levels = 16 codebooks of 1024 entries) |
| Audio features | 128 mel bands at 24 kHz, FFT 1024, hop 256 |
| Training data | Song Describer Dataset and JamendoLyrics MultiLang |
| License | CC BY-SA 4.0, subject to the upstream dataset terms |

## Checkpoints

The step values are exactly what each `model.json` records. `best/` is the weight-only checkpoint selected by validation. `latest/` is the resumable checkpoint with AdamW moments. Some early runs stored only `best/`, and `thor-base` and `smoke` record step 0 in their `best/model.json`. Where a `latest/` exists, prefer it for the late training state.

### About `pq-large`

`pq-large` is still training on the Jetson AGX Thor (128 GB). The files here are a snapshot at step 7,000 of 20,000, and they will be replaced as the run advances. Its validation loss (5.135 nats per token at step 7,000) is averaged over 16 codebooks of a different tokenizer, so it cannot be compared directly with the 4-codebook runs above.

The model reads codes from the band-group tokenizer, which splits the 128 mel bands into 4 groups and quantises each group with 4 residual levels. That tokenizer is stored as `checkpoints/pq-large/tokenizer.json`, and the matching caches are `cache-g4l4f1/`, `cache-pq-jamendolyrics/` and `cache-pq-recordings/` in the dataset repository. Pass `--cache data/cache-g4l4f1` when generating with this run.

`evaluations/<run>/` holds the paired lyrics test of each lyrics run: the per-track loss with aligned, removed and mismatched lyrics.

## Training progress

The runs on the Jetson AGX Thor publish their metrics here every two hours
(`deploy/hf/publish.sh` in the code repository): `metrics/<run>.jsonl` holds
every logged event, and `plots/<run>.png` shows, from left to right, the
training and validation loss in nats per code against optimizer step, the
latest validation loss of each codebook (coarse levels are far easier to
predict than fine ones), and the throughput in positions per second.

![pq-large training curves](plots/pq-large.png)

## Layout

```text
checkpoints/<run>/best/      weights only       model.json + tensors.bin
checkpoints/<run>/latest/    weights + AdamW    model.json + tensors.bin
configs/                     canonical training configurations
run-configs/                 per-run config.json where the run saved one
metrics/                     full metrics.jsonl for every run
logs/                        captured training logs and the tokenizer sweeps
evaluations/<run>/           paired lyrics evaluations
```

`tensors.bin` is little-endian `f32` in parameter-visitor order. `latest/` appends the AdamW first moments and then the second moments. `model.json` records the tensor manifest, the step, whether optimizer state is present, and the training configuration.

## Download and use

```bash
hf download arpanpathak/staleynet-checkpoints \
  --repo-type model --local-dir staleynet-checkpoints

# From the code repository, on a Jetson with the cuda-oxide toolchain:
cargo oxide build -- --release
staleynet sing \
  --cache data/cache \
  --run staleynet-checkpoints/checkpoints/thor-base/best \
  --prompt "slow acoustic ballad, warm female voice" \
  --out song.wav
```

For the lyrics model:

```bash
staleynet sing \
  --run staleynet-checkpoints/checkpoints/lyrics-orin/best \
  --prompt "grunge rock, raw male voice" \
  --lyrics-file song.txt \
  --out song.wav
```

Architecture: width 256, 8 heads, 6 layers, feed-forward multiplier 4, context length 768, 4 residual codebooks of 1024 entries, 128 mel bands at 24 kHz. `lyrics-orin` adds a 256-byte lyrics field.

- **Song Describer Dataset** (SDD), Zenodo record [10072001](https://zenodo.org/records/10072001): 706 Jamendo recordings with human captions. Captions are CC BY-SA 4.0. The recordings carry the per-track Creative Commons licenses in `audio_licenses.txt`, including CC BY-NC-ND and CC BY-NC-SA.

The CUDA port carries over growing AR buffers, cached NAR prefixes, bounded NAR windows
(1024 frames / 128 overlap), and deferred packed-weight uploads from the B70 work.
CUDA Flash Attention and CUDA graphs replace Intel-specific kernels. An independent, opt-in streaming
pipeline overlaps safe NAR weight loading with earlier work and preserves the tested predecessor PCM.
The measured full-song runtime stays frozen; streaming has its own binary and source identity.
The older engine ignores `yue2.packed_projections` and `yue2.kv_cache_alignment` request keys:
they are retained where present in raw historical receipts, but receive no performance credit.

# YuE2-3B · IRA and IRAE merges

> Ruach Studio is open music generation that runs on your own hardware: the model, the score, the adapters and every take stay yours, and nothing is rented by the token. Open models are now good enough to stand on their own, and what was missing is the studio around them: that is what we build, in the open. Music should be free to make and to share: whoever has no voice, no instrument and no studio still has the right to lay their thoughts and feelings onto sound.

> **⚠ Not on free cloud GPUs.** Ruach Studio does not run on Google Colab, Kaggle or any free notebook GPU, so don't spend an evening on it there: it is a whole studio, not a notebook. It builds its C++/CUDA engine on the machine it lives on, keeps a server and a lab of Python services running beside it, and takes about 33 GB of disk (60 GB with the Artist). A free session's card, memory, wiped disk and hours-long limit cannot hold that. It wants your own Linux computer, or a server you rent and keep, with an NVIDIA card: 24 GB for everything, 16 GB with the smaller model copies. The weights on this page load wherever YuE2-3B does, ComfyUI among them: the warning is about the studio.

**IRA** stands for **I**nstrumental + **R**eal **A**udio. Two community LoRAs are folded into the weights of [m-a-p's YuE2-3B](https://huggingface.co/m-a-p/YuE2-3B), so the model plays them with no adapter loaded. The merge was made and checked in [Ruach Studio](https://github.com/igrbible/Ruach_Studio), a free studio built on YuE2 ([its page](https://ruachstudio.art)).

| adapter | author | half of YuE2 | strength |
|---|---|---|---|
| [YuE2-instrumental-cot-full-loras](https://huggingface.co/Mothersuperior/YuE2-instrumental-cot-full-loras) · `ar_lora_inst_v3abc` | Mothersuperior | music (AR: the score and the music tokens) | 0.75 |
| [yue2-mothersuperior-realaudio-tokenizer-v4](https://huggingface.co/Mothersuperior/yue2-mothersuperior-realaudio-tokenizer-v4) · `nar_lora_joint_v9` | Mothersuperior | sound (NAR: the decoder of the latents) | 0.85 |

The Instrumental adapter gives the music half a feel for arrangement and section plans. The Real Audio adapter moves the sound half toward real-production recordings.

## IRAE: IRA with an epic-trailer adapter

**IRAE** is IRA plus [monsterovich's Epic Trailer adapter](https://huggingface.co/monsterovich/yue2-steps-from-hell) (`yue2-steps-from-hell`: a music-half file, `adapter-ar-195`, and a sound-half file, `adapter-nar-194`). Three strengths, all heard and kept:

| merge | Epic Trailer, music / sound | by ear |
|---|---|---|
| **IRAE** | 0.32 / 0.32 | the best of the three |
| **IRAEv2** | 0.28 / 0.24 | cleaner |
| **IRAEv3** | 0.5 / 0.375, the strengths its author recommends | more grain in the voice; at its best on instrumentals |

Every IRAE carries IRA whole (Instrumental 0.75 on the music half, Real Audio v9 0.85 on the sound half). All four adapters were added in one pass from the stock BF16, in F32, exactly as IRA was made.

- **Measured:** the Epic Trailer's music half at 1.0 broke every score (9 plans out of 9 had no key line). At 0.5 and below the scores held (18 out of 18 for IRAEv2 and IRAEv3). Its sound half raised the hiss in the quietest fifth even at 0.32–0.4, and the ear still preferred it.
- **Do not load Epic Trailer again on top of an IRAE,** nor Instrumental or Real Audio: they are inside.

## IRAE-IR and IRAE-IRv2: experimental, for rock instrumentals

> ⚠ **Highly unstable on lyrics. Experimental: mostly for rock instrumentals.**

**IRAE-IR** is IRAE plus [monsterovich's Industrial Rock adapter](https://huggingface.co/monsterovich/yue2-industrial-rock-lora) (`yue2-industrial-rock-lora`: a music-half file, `adapter-ar-179`, and a sound-half file, `adapter-nar-179-v2`). Each carries IRAE whole (IRA plus Epic Trailer 0.32 / 0.32); all six adapters were added in one pass from the stock BF16, in F32.

| merge | Industrial Rock, music / sound | by ear |
|---|---|---|
| **IRAE-IR** | 0.4 / 0.6 | richer than IRA and IRAE, with the rock colour the adapter brings, and raw rock sounds good; the words are what suffers: the phonetics get worse, the voice can drown in the band, a ballad can lose words and its feel. A sung poem over a duduk came out well |
| **IRAE-IRv2** | 0.32 / 0.6 | the music half lowered further for steadier words; made after that verdict, not yet heard |

- **Measured:** Industrial Rock's music half at 0.6 broke two plans out of seven (no key line); its limit measured at 0.45, and both merges stay under it.
- **Do not load Industrial Rock again on top,** nor Epic Trailer, Instrumental or Real Audio: they are inside.

## Files

| file | for | size |
|---|---|---|
| `model.safetensors` + `config.json`, `modeling_yue2.py`, `qwen.tiktoken`, the generation configs | anything that loads m-a-p/YuE2-3B (Transformers with `trust_remote_code`, ComfyUI conversions, your own code): the same layout and names, BF16 | 7.3 GB |
| `YuE2-3B-IRA-BF16.gguf` | [yue2.cpp](https://github.com/ServeurpersoCom/yue2.cpp) and Ruach Studio, the whole merge | 7.2 GB |
| `YuE2-3B-IRA-Q8_0.gguf` | the same, quantized from the merged BF16 | 3.8 GB |
| `YuE2-3B-IRA-Q6_K.gguf` | the same, smaller | 2.9 GB |

The three IRAE merges sit beside IRA in the same three GGUF sizes: `YuE2-3B-IRAE-BF16.gguf`, `YuE2-3B-IRAE-Q8_0.gguf`, `YuE2-3B-IRAE-Q6_K.gguf`, and the same for `IRAEv2`, `IRAEv3`, `IRAE-IR` and `IRAE-IRv2`. Their safetensors are in the folders `IRAE/`, `IRAEv2/`, `IRAEv3/`, `IRAE-IR/` and `IRAE-IRv2/`, each in m-a-p's layout: load one with `subfolder="IRAE"`.

The VAE is not part of this repo. Use m-a-p's [YuE2-Vae](https://huggingface.co/m-a-p/YuE2-Vae) as before; in GGUF form it is in [Serveurperso/YuE2-GGUF](https://huggingface.co/Serveurperso/YuE2-GGUF).

**Do not load these two adapters again on top of IRA.** They are already inside, and loading them again would double them. Other adapters stack as usual.

## How it was merged

- Both adapters were taken in their fp32 files (`ar_lora_inst_v3abc.safetensors`, `nar_lora_joint_v9.safetensors`), not their bf16 copies: they are only merged, never loaded, so the larger file costs nothing.
- Each LoRA pair was added as `W + strength × alpha/rank × B @ A` in F32 and stored back in BF16. The arithmetic is yue2.cpp's own LoRA merge (its `lora.h`): the merged BF16 GGUF loads into the same weights as the stock model with these two adapters at these strengths at load time.
- Real Audio ships full `vae2llm` / `llm2vae` weights rather than a low-rank pair. At 0.85 they enter as `base + 0.85 × (theirs − base)`, as yue2.cpp applies them.
- The quants were made from the merged BF16 (yue2.cpp's `quantize`), not by merging into a quant.
- `model.safetensors` is m-a-p's own file with the 396 merged tensors taken from the BF16 GGUF. It was checked tensor by tensor after writing: the 2-D weights are the GGUF's bit for bit, and the two biases are rounded to BF16 as m-a-p stores them.

## What we measured (preliminary)

These are first numbers from two prompts, an epic instrumental and a sung Russian ballad, taken on RTX 3090s in October 2026. They are a start, not a verdict.

- **Exactness.** The merged BF16 GGUF and the stock BF16 with the two adapters at runtime gave the same audio and the same latents, byte for byte (same score, same seeds).
- **The score holds.** Three prompts × three seeds on the BF16, the Q8_0 and the Q6_K all wrote a valid ABC score (key, meter, note length): 36 plans, none broken. Only the music half writes the score, and it is the same in IRA and in the neighbouring recipe whose quants were planned (Real Audio at 0.9).
- **Sound.** The hiss in the quietest fifth of each take was not above the stock model's, and the 2–6 kHz share stayed at 1–4 % of the energy. Recipes that carried an epic-trailer adapter raised both, even at 0.32–0.4.
- **By ear.** Approved for release. It is strongest on sung songs; a pure instrumental can carry a little noise.

If you hear it differently, tell us. The numbers are ours, not laws.

## Use

- **Ruach Studio:** Engine › Models and LoRAs › More models › «IRA merge» (and, from 2.0.0, «IRAE», «IRAEv2», «IRAEv3», «IRAE-IR», «IRAE-IRv2») fetches a GGUF. Engine › Compute then chooses it beside m-a-p's weights.
- **yue2.cpp:** pass the GGUF as the backbone (`--model YuE2-3B-IRA-Q8_0.gguf`), with the stock VAE.
- **Transformers and other shells:** load this repo as you load `m-a-p/YuE2-3B`.

- [monsterovich](https://huggingface.co/monsterovich) for the Epic Trailer adapter in every IRAE and the [Industrial Rock adapter](https://huggingface.co/monsterovich/yue2-industrial-rock-lora) in IRAE-IR and IRAE-IRv2. His word on them: «I'm not opposed to any use of them, including commercial use. Just make sure to credit the author».
- [Serveurperso](https://huggingface.co/Serveurperso) for [yue2.cpp](https://github.com/ServeurpersoCom/yue2.cpp), its GGUF format, its LoRA merge and its quantizer.

- The merge, the checks and the measurements were done in [Ruach Studio](https://github.com/igrbible/Ruach_Studio).

The weights derive from YuE2-3B and keep its licence: [CC BY-NC 4.0](https://creativecommons.org/licenses/by-nc/4.0/), non-commercial use, with credit as above. `LICENSE`, `THIRD_PARTY_NOTICES.md` and `licenses/` are m-a-p's, copied unchanged.

Sophon-Realtime v1

An open full-duplex voice model that hears your tone and speaks with one.
Adventists AI · Apache-2.0

GitHub · ModelScope · 中文

## Highlights - **VoiceBench 82.8 and Big Bench Audio 81.8%: the strongest brain among open full-duplex models.** #1 among open full-duplex models on both; level with GPT-4o-mini-Audio on VoiceBench. - **Paralinguistic understanding 48.6, #1 overall: it hears your tone.** Ahead of Gemini 3.8 Flash (46.9) and Qwen3-Omni (44.6) on LISTEN, StressTest and MSPB. It hears emotion, emphasis, sarcasm, laughter and sighs straight from your voice. - **NVV-SuperBench 0.74 (Chinese) and 0.68 (English): it speaks with tone.** The baseline without expression scores 0.37 / 0.27. The model decides from the conversation when to laugh, when to sigh, and when to clear a dry throat. - **Starts talking about 0.4 s after you stop: it's fast.** It listens the whole time you talk and drafts its reply as you go. It picks up as soon as you stop, and when you cut in it stops and answers your new question. - **Full-Duplex-Bench v3 tool calling: Pass@1 48%, ahead of Grok (43%), and 100% response rate: it gets work done.** Live mode lets it work together with a larger backend model, and it is compatible with the OpenAI GPT-Live interface format. Text and voice stream together, so every reply comes with an auditable transcript. - **Runs on a single GPU: yours to deploy.** A quantized build runs on a single consumer GPU. Apache-2.0 code and weights, free for commercial use. ## Benchmark details ### Conversation: VoiceBench (official evaluators, gpt-4o-mini judge) | model | full-duplex | open weights | overall | |---|:-:|:-:|:-:| | GPT-4o-Audio | — | — | 86.8 | | **Sophon-Realtime v1** | ✅ | ✅ | **82.8** | | GPT-4o-mini-Audio | — | — | 82.8 | | MiniCPM-o 4.5 | ✅ | ✅ | 76.1 | | MiniCPM-o 2.6 | ✅ | ✅ | 71.2 | | Freeze-Omni | ✅ | ✅ | 55.2 | | NemotronLabs VoiceChat | ✅ | ✅ | 55.1 | | PersonaPlex | ✅ | ✅ | 30.6 | | Moshi | ✅ | ✅ | 29.5 | AlpacaEval uses the 199-question standard subset. Other scores come from the VoiceBench leaderboard and from Table 3 of the NemotronLabs VoiceChat paper (arXiv:2609.21967); the MiniCPM-o 4.5 score there is from an independent evaluation. ### Spoken reasoning: Big Bench Audio 1,000 spoken reasoning questions, graded on what the model actually says. | model | open weights | accuracy | |---|:-:|:-:| | GPT-Live-1 | — | 90% | | **Sophon-Realtime v1** | ✅ | **81.8%** | | Raon SpeechChat | ✅ | 58% | | Freeze-Omni | ✅ | 33% | | PersonaPlex | ✅ | 19% | | Moshi | ✅ | 4% | Sophon: self-run, with spoken answers transcribed and judged by gpt-4.1. Others: Artificial Analysis leaderboard. ### Tool calling: Full-Duplex-Bench v3 Disfluent real human speech with multi-step tool calls. 100 tasks, judged by GPT-4o. | model | open weights | Pass@1 ↑ | responds when it should ↑ | |---|:-:|:-:|:-:| | GPT-Realtime | — | 60% | 96% | | Gemini Live 3.1 | — | 54% | — | | **Sophon-Realtime** | ✅ | **48%** | **100%** | | cascaded pipeline | — | 45% | — | | Grok | — | 43% | — | | Ultravox v0.7 | ✅ | 41% | — | Sophon: best of several runs (internal baseline configuration). Others: official Full-Duplex-Bench v3 results. ### Hearing tone: paralinguistic understanding Sophon-Realtime listens with [DuplexJev](https://huggingface.co/adventists-ai/DuplexJev-32B-Para). These benchmarks test emotion, sarcasm, stress and intonation. | model | LISTEN (4 tasks) + StressTest + MSPB, combined | |---|:-:| | **DuplexJev (Sophon-Realtime's ears)** | **48.6** | | Gemini 3.8 Flash | 46.9 | | Qwen3-Omni | 44.6 | ### Speaking with tone: NVV-SuperBench Checks whether the laughs, coughs, sighs and breaths a reply calls for actually show up in the audio. Official scripts, 50 items per category, judged by Gemini 3 Flash; higher F1 is better. | model | Chinese | English | |---|:-:|:-:| | **Sophon-Realtime v1** | **0.74** | **0.68** | | internal baseline without expression | 0.37 | 0.27 | ## How it works - **A vector language hidden inside the model.** We found that the stream of continuous vectors a speech LLM builds while it listens is a complete language in its own right. A frozen LLM reads it as easily as text, and it carries both what was said and how it was said: intonation, emphasis and emotion. Sophon-Realtime v1's voice writes this vector language directly, then turns it back into sound. Hearing and speaking share one representation, so the tone the model can hear is the tone it can speak. - **Listens continuously.** At each pause, the same model decides in a single token whether you've finished, are still talking, are back-channeling or are thinking. - **Drafts early, speaks on time.** A reply is drafted from your first pause and released the moment the model decides it's its turn. If you keep talking, the draft is dropped before you hear it. - **Remembers what you actually heard.** History keeps the real audio of both sides. When you interrupt, only the part you heard is kept. ## Deployment Runs on a single GPU; a quantized build runs on a single consumer GPU. ```bash pip install sophon-realtime hf download adventists-ai/Sophon-Realtime-v1 --local-dir Sophon-Realtime-v1 # launch commands: see deploy/ in the GitHub repository ``` The server is compatible with the OpenAI GPT-Live interface format, so existing realtime voice clients can connect directly. ## License Code and weights are released under Apache-2.0. Third-party components keep their own licences; see NOTICE. ## Contact Business enquiries: jiejin@adventists.ai

# Whisper tiny.en, hand-edited to stop writing words on silence

An unofficial, hand-edited version of [`openai/whisper-tiny.en`](https://huggingface.co/openai/whisper-tiny.en). It wasn't
retrained: 3,845 of its 37.8 million weights were changed by hand.

On audio with nobody speaking, such as silence, hiss, hum, tones or noise, the original writes words. With greedy decoding it's
almost always "you", and with the pipeline's beam search it's often looping sentences like "I'm going to do it. I'm going to do
it." This version writes a lone "." instead. Its transcripts of real speech are as accurate as before.

On real recordings of everyday sounds it's less complete. It cuts the recordings that get words by about 80%, but it still
writes words over many animal and human sounds, such as crying, laughter or a cat (see Results).

**Made with WSP Lab, coming soon: [join the waitlist at wsp-lab.ai](https://wsp-lab.ai/?utm_source=huggingface&utm_medium=model-card&utm_campaign=whisper-tiny)**

WSP Lab is a tool that lets AI agents edit a model's weights directly, quickly and verifiably. This edit used its approach,
with a purpose-built harness.

## How long it took

| Step | Wall-clock time | Done by |
|---|---|---|
| Rules, pre-registration and a short investigation of the model | 15 min | Claude Opus 5.5 |
| **The edit, from brief to a tested edit** | **40 min** | **Claude Fable 5.1**, one of three editors working in parallel |
| Waiting for the slowest of the three editors | 23 min | |
| Choosing between the edits and scoring them on the final split | 8 min | Claude Opus 5.5 |
| Independent audit, including the beam-search checks that changed which edit was released | 50 min | Claude Opus 5.5, with the switch decided by the model's owner |
| Release | 1 min to this upload | Claude Opus 5.5 |

- **Total:** 2 hours 17 minutes from the start of the run to the upload, on one laptop (an Apple M5 Max), with no training. It
  was 2 hours 19 minutes to the download check below.
- **Download check:** downloaded with no login into an empty cache, it wrote no words on 400 fresh non-speech clips, with either
  decoding. Its greedy transcripts of those clips and of 100 utterances matched the experiment's exactly.
- **Budget:** the edit used 2 test runs of about 20 seconds each. Most of the 40 minutes went to the agent's reasoning, not to
  compute.
- **Timing source:** every time above comes from the experiment's own logs and file timestamps, on 6 and 7 November 2026.

## Results

All numbers are on held-out data that the editors never saw.
- **Non-speech:** seeded synthetic 10-second clips, of 8 kinds (digital silence, hiss, white noise, rumble, mains hum, tones,
  chords and clicks).
- **Speech:** 820 LibriSpeech test-clean utterances (items 1,800 to 2,619, sorted by id), scored with Whisper's English text
  normaliser.

A clip counts as a hallucination if its transcript contains any letter or digit.

| Decoding | Model | Non-speech clips with words | LibriSpeech WER |
|---|---|---|---|
| Greedy, which `model.generate()` uses | **This model** | **0.0%** of 4,000 | **6.375%** |
| | The original | 89.7% | 6.375% |
| 5-beam search, which `pipeline()` uses by default | **This model** | **0.0%** of 1,000 | **5.500%** |
| | The original | 23.0% | 5.531% |

Paired differences on the same utterances, with 95% bootstrap intervals:
- **Greedy:** WER **+0.000 points** (−0.037 to +0.032). 10 of the 820 transcripts changed: 2 got better and 3 worse.
- **5-beam search:** WER **−0.031 points** (−0.068 to −0.006).

**Sounds nobody tested during editing.** There were 592 clips:
- 200 instrumental music loops;
- the 14 macOS alert sounds, each at 3 positions in silence;
- 350 clips of 7 new noise types (pink, brown, chirps, square waves, band-passed, modulated and speech-shaped).

| Decoding | The original | This model | Music | Alert sounds | New noise types |
|---|---|---|---|---|---|
| Greedy | 97.3% | **2.9%** | 1.5% | 33% | 0% |
| 5-beam search | 65.9% | **1.0%** | 1.0% | 9.5% | 0% |

The last three columns are this model's rate on each kind of sound.

**Harder speech,** with greedy decoding: under white noise at 10 dB SNR, quieted by 26 dB, after 8 seconds of silence, and after
5 seconds of hiss, every WER change was within ±0.08 points. 2 of the 820 quiet utterances came out as "." (see Limits).

**Timestamp mode** (`return_timestamps=True`): words on non-speech fell from 49.1% to 0%, and WER changed by −0.037 points.

**Long recordings,** tested after the release. There were 273 recordings of about 2.5 minutes, each with 3 LibriSpeech utterances
and stretches of 5 to 60 seconds of generated noise or silence around them, and 50 recordings of 90 seconds of non-speech only.

| Decoding | Non-speech recordings with words | Inserted words per 100 spoken | WER |
|---|---|---|---|
| `pipeline(chunk_length_s=30)` | 34% → **4%** | 29.5 → **1.0** | 40.2% → **11.2%** |
| `pipeline(return_timestamps=True)` | 100% → **6%** | 853 → **106** | 859% → **112%** |
| `generate(return_timestamps=True)`, greedy | 94% → **6%** | 12.8 → 12.2 | 19.4% → 18.7% |

Each cell is the original, then this model. It missed no more of the spoken words in any of the three. For long audio, use
`chunk_length_s=30`:
- sequential decoding through the pipeline loops badly with either model;
- with greedy sequential `generate()`, this edit doesn't stop hallucinations in recordings that also contain speech.

**Real recorded sounds,** tested after the release on [ESC-50](https://github.com/karolpiczak/ESC-50): 2,000 five-second
recordings of 50 kinds of everyday sound, from rain and engines to dogs, crying babies and laughter.

| Decoding | The original | This model | Natural sounds and water | Urban noises | Domestic sounds | Animals | Human sounds |
|---|---|---|---|---|---|---|---|
| Greedy | 96.7% | **19.6%** | 3.0% | 5.0% | 8.0% | 34.3% | 47.5% |
| 5-beam search | 87.4% | **19.1%** | 2.3% | 4.5% | 7.3% | 35.8% | 45.8% |

The last five columns are this model's rate on each group of 400 recordings.
- **It works on noise-like sounds.** It wrote no words on any recording of rain, waves, wind, fire, engines, trains, airplanes or
  washing machines.
- **It fails on voice-like sounds:** crying babies (98%), sneezing (90%), laughter (85%), cats (83%) and roosters (70%). The
  original's own no-speech signal is unsure on these too.
  - Some of what it writes, like "Ha ha ha" over laughter, can be defended as transcription.
  - Much can't, like "I'm so sorry." over laughter.
- **Real sounds under speech don't trip it.** One of these recordings was mixed under each of the 820 test utterances, at 10, 5
  and 0 dB SNR. It blanked none of them, and every WER change was between −0.31 and −0.01 points, with no interval above zero.

## Compared with a rule in the decoder

The original already computes the signal this edit uses: its probability of "no captions" (token 50361) at the first decoding
position. OpenAI's own `transcribe()` reads it to skip silent segments. So, after the release, the original was also scored with
two rules in the decoder, on the same held-out data:

| Model | Non-speech with words, greedy | 5-beam search | Unseen sounds, greedy | 5-beam search | Speech WER change, greedy and beams |
|---|---|---|---|---|---|
| **This model** | **0.0%** | **0.0%** | 2.9% | **1.0%** | +0.000 and −0.031 |
| The original, skipping when that probability is above 0.5 | 0.1% | 0.0% | 2.5% | 2.4% | +0.000 and +0.000 |
| The original with OpenAI's default rule: above 0.6, with an average log-probability below −1.0 | 13.6% | 15.7% | 14.9% | 35.6% | +0.000 and +0.000 |
| The original | 89.7% | 23.0% | 97.3% | 65.9% | |

- **If you can change your decoding code,** the plain threshold does about as well, and it outputs an empty string rather than
  ".". It skipped no real speech in any test, where this model blanked 4 short or quiet clips.
- **On real recorded sounds** (ESC-50, above), the threshold and this model do about the same, 19.3% and 19.6% with greedy
  decoding, and fail on the same kinds of sound. Neither skipped any utterance with those sounds under speech.
- **OpenAI's default rule does much worse.** It also needs the transcript to look unconfident, and these hallucinations often
  aren't: it keeps " you" on every clip of digital silence. On the real recordings it leaves words on 40.8%.
- **transformers 5.22.2's built-in version,** `generate(no_speech_threshold=0.6, logprob_threshold=-1.0)`, fails with greedy
  decoding, and with beams it skipped none of 16 test clips.
- **What this model adds** is that it needs no code: it works in `pipeline()` and `generate()` as they are.

## What was changed

The original already knows when nobody is speaking, at least on generated noise. At the first decoding position, its own "no
captions" prediction separates speech from generated noise perfectly, but the first word is chosen one position later, and that
prediction isn't used there. The edit carries the signal across, in three steps, each built to stay exactly zero on speech:

1. **Detect.** Two unused units in decoder layer 2's MLP (267 and 718) form a soft step. It reads the model's own "no captions"
   direction at the first position and fires above a threshold. When it fires, it writes a marker direction, borrowed from a
   decoder position embedding (447) that decoding never reaches.
2. **Carry.** One value channel (dimension 145) of attention head 2 in decoder layer 3 carries the marker forward. That head
   already looks mostly at the first position.
3. **Act.** Two unused units in decoder layer 3's MLP (1426 and 621) form a second step. When the marker arrives, they raise " ."
   and end-of-text and lower " you" and " You".

Whisper's decoding config won't let the model end at its first token, so on non-speech it writes " ." and then ends. Every
direction used comes from the model's own weights, and every number was chosen by hand. On 1,620 held-out utterances the detector
and the final step were exactly zero at all 41,984 decoding positions.

The edit can only be as good as the signal it carries. On real animal and human sounds, the original's "no captions" prediction
is unsure, so the edit misses many of those.

`edit.safetensors` holds just the 9 changed tensors. `model.safetensors` is the complete model.

## Usage

```python
import numpy as np
from transformers import pipeline

asr = pipeline("automatic-speech-recognition", model="erickvs/whisper-tiny.en-hand-edited")

print(asr("speech.wav")["text"])  # transcribes as usual
print(asr("long_recording.wav", chunk_length_s=30)["text"])  # for audio over 30 seconds

noise = (0.05 * np.random.default_rng(0).standard_normal(16000 * 10)).astype(np.float32)  # 10 s of white noise
print(asr({"raw": noise, "sampling_rate": 16000})["text"])  # " ."; the original writes " I'm going to do it. I'm going to do it. ..."
```

To apply just the edit to the original weights:

```python
from huggingface_hub import hf_hub_download
from safetensors.torch import load_file
from transformers import WhisperForConditionalGeneration

model = WhisperForConditionalGeneration.from_pretrained("openai/whisper-tiny.en")
edit = load_file(hf_hub_download("erickvs/whisper-tiny.en-hand-edited", "edit.safetensors"))
model.load_state_dict(edit, strict=False)  # replaces 9 tensors and leaves the rest untouched
```

It was tested with transformers 5.22.2 and torch 2.15.0, on Apple's MPS backend, in float32.

## Limits

- **It writes "." rather than nothing.** Whisper's generation config blocks end-of-text as the first token, so the shortest
  possible transcript is one token. Strip a lone "." if you need an empty string.
- **Real sounds.** On real recordings it still writes words on about 1 in 5, mostly over animal and human sounds such as crying,
  laughter, sneezing, cats and roosters. With greedy decoding, a third of the macOS alert sounds still get words too. Crowds,
  rooms and music with singing haven't been tested.
- **Rare false alarms.** The decision is made at the start of each 30-second window, where its margin on speech is small: 12.76 at
  the most on held-out speech, against a threshold of 12.93. It turned 2 of 820 test utterances quieted by 26 dB into ".". Both
  were one- or two-word replies, "Indeed." and "Quick, quick.". It did the same to 2 of 820 three-second fragments of speech.
- **Speech coverage:** read English from LibriSpeech only, clean or with white noise or real recordings mixed underneath. Other
  accents, conversational speech and speech recorded in noisy places haven't been tested. Long recordings were tested only with
  generated noise between utterances (see Results).
- **One base model:** the numbers were chosen for `whisper-tiny.en`, and they won't carry over to other Whisper sizes.
- **Comparison:** Calm-Whisper (2025) cut such hallucinations by more than 80% by fine-tuning. This edit wasn't compared with it on
  the same data.

## How it was made

The model comes from an experiment in editing neural networks by hand, with no training. Three AI editors (Claude Fable 5.1, by
Anthropic) worked independently under the same fixed rules. Those banned gradients, optimizers, fitting weights to data, automated
search and weights from other models. Each editor had 40 test runs on development data. A separate selection split was used to
choose between the finished edits, and a final split, which no editor could run, gave one final score. The bar was set before
any edit existed: cut non-speech hallucinations by at least 80%, with LibriSpeech word error no worse by a paired bootstrap
interval.

**This isn't the edit the pre-registered rule picked.** The rule picked a different editor's edit. It was even cleaner with greedy
decoding (no held-out transcript changed), but under `pipeline()`'s default 5-beam search it made hallucinations worse than the
original's: 97% against 23%. The audit found this after the final scores were in. This edit also met the bar on the final split,
and it holds under both kinds of decoding, so it was released instead. The switch rests on the selection split, not the final one.
There, under 5-beam search, the pick wrote words on 97.2% of non-speech clips, where the original wrote them on 22.8%. This edit
wrote them on none, with a WER change of +0.025 points (−0.013 to +0.071). The third edit failed the speech condition there.

An independent audit recomputed the headline numbers from the raw transcripts, checked that the edit file holds only what its
author described, and tested its explanation on held-out data. The full write-up, including the other two edits and everything
that went wrong, is in the experiment notes.

## Support the experiments

These experiments run on one laptop, but the AI agents that make and audit the edits cost real money: the three editors behind this
release used about 830,000 tokens. If you'd like more models fixed by hand like this one, published with their full results and
limits, you can **[support the experiments on Patreon](https://www.patreon.com/c/ErickVazquezSantillan)**. It pays
for the tokens behind the next ones.

# KurisuMakiseTTS — 牧濑红莉栖 中文/日语 TTS 微调模型

基于 **GPT-SoVITS v5**（dev / turbo 双版本）微调的角色语音模型。

## 快速开始

### 1. 准备 GPT-SoVITS 环境

```bash
git clone https://github.com/RVC-Boss/GPT-SoVITS.git
cd GPT-SoVITS
pip install -r requirements.txt
```

### 2. 下载必需的基座模型

以下模型**不在本仓库内**，请从官方获取，放到 `GPT-SoVITS/GPT_SoVITS/pretrained_models/`：

| 文件 | 用途 | 来源 |
|---|---|---|
| `chinese-hubert-base/` | 音频特征 | `TencentGameMate/chinese-hubert-base` |
| `chinese-roberta-wwm-ext-large/` | 文本特征 | `hfl/chinese-roberta-wwm-ext-large` |
| `s1v3.ckpt` | GPT 基座 | `lj1995/GPT-SoVITS` |
| `gsv-v5-pretrained/s2Gv5dev.pth` | dev 版 SoVITS 基座 | 同上 |
| `gsv-v5-pretrained/s2Gv5turbo.pth` | turbo 版 SoVITS 基座 | 同上 |
| `gsv-v5-pretrained/vocoder.pth` | 声码器 | 同上 |
| `sv/pretrained_eres2netv2w24s4ep4.ckpt` | 说话人验证 | 同上 |

### 3. 放置本模型

```
GPT-SoVITS/GPT_SoVITS/pretrained_models/
└── kurisu/
    ├── kurisu_v5_gpt.ckpt
    ├── kurisu_v5_sovits.pth
    └── kurisu_v5turbo_sovits.pth
```

### 4. 配置并启动

用 `config/` 下的模板，把路径改成你的实际路径：

```bash
# dev 版
python api_v2.py -a 127.0.0.1 -p 9880 -c config/tts_infer_v5dev.yaml

# turbo 版
python api_v2.py -a 127.0.0.1 -p 9880 -c config/tts_infer_v5turbo.yaml
```

### 5. 合成

```bash
curl http://127.0.0.1:9880/tts -H "Content-Type: application/json" -d '{
  "text": "早上好，我是牧濑红莉栖。",
  "text_lang": "zh",
  "ref_audio_path": "ref_audio/ref1.wav",
  "prompt_text": "あなたに会いに来たの、岡部凛太郎さん。じゃなくて…",
  "prompt_lang": "ja",
  "media_type": "wav"
}' -o out.wav
```

> **参考音频是必需的**——GPT-SoVITS 架构上参考音频参与推理（音色锚点 + 韵律起点）。
> 但音色已经微调进权重，所以换参考音频主要影响**语气**，而不是"像不像"。

---

## 参考音频建议

`ref_audio/` 提供 3 条 5–6 秒的干净样本。挑选原则：

- **5–10 秒**，不要超过 10 秒（api_v2 会拒绝）
- 干净、无 BGM、无混响
- **想要什么语气就选什么语气的样本**——合成会继承参考的语气
- `prompt_text` 必须和音频内容**逐字一致**

这批素材以「理性陈述」为主（占比约 73%），情绪化样本较少，这是选型时的客观限制。

# Africa TTS

Fast text-to-speech for **92 African languages and English**, with voice cloning, faster than real time on a CPU: runs on audio.cpp by default (**144 MB, no PyTorch, first streamed audio after about 0.1 s**), 110M parameters.

🎙️ [**Try it live**](https://huggingface.co/spaces/AfriSpeech/africa-tts-demo) · 🔊 [Samples in 53 languages](https://huggingface.co/spaces/AfriSpeech/africa-tts-samples) · 💻 [Code, server, mobile](https://github.com/AfriSpeech/africa-tts)

## Quick start

```bash
pip install africa-tts   # English also needs espeak-ng
```

```python
from africa_tts import AfricaTTS

tts = AfricaTTS.load()
audio = tts.generate("Akwaaba! Yɛfrɛ me Kofi.", lang="twi")              # default Twi voice
audio = tts.generate("Hello Ghana!", lang="eng", voice="my_voice.wav")  # clone a 3-10 s clip
tts.save(audio, "out.wav")
```

The default engine is [audio.cpp](https://github.com/0xShug0/audio.cpp) on the CPU (the q8_0 GGUF in
[gguf/](https://huggingface.co/AfriSpeech/africa-tts/tree/main/gguf), no PyTorch);
`pip install "africa-tts[torch]"` adds the unquantised PyTorch engine, also on a GPU. The first
run asks before downloading the model (about 150 MB), then works offline. Output: 24 kHz mono.
Every language has a default voice. Spell out numbers. Plain pocket-tts works too, with IPA
input: [see how](https://github.com/AfriSpeech/africa-tts/blob/main/docs/MODEL.md#using-plain-pocket-tts).

## Benchmark

Each system reads the same held-out sentences (Omnilingual ASR corpus, FLEURS, WAXAL, FLORES+;
none in our training data), and [Omnilingual ASR](https://huggingface.co/facebook/omniASR-LLM-7B)
transcribes the audio: a lower **character error rate (CER)** means more intelligible speech.
On the 27 languages both support (at least 10 test sentences each), Africa TTS has the lower
error rate than MMS-TTS in 21:

![CER per language, Africa TTS vs MMS-TTS: lower is better](assets/benchmark_cer.png)

Africa TTS uses each language's default voice; MMS-TTS uses its own voices.

## Model

- 6-layer [Pocket TTS](https://github.com/kyutai-labs/pocket-tts) FlowLM (110M parameters with the Mimi codec), distilled with Kyutai's `depth_distill` recipe from the guided 24-layer [Africa TTS Base](https://huggingface.co/AfriSpeech/africa-tts-base), so guidance is in its weights; 200k steps.
- Reads IPA from [africa-g2p](https://github.com/AfriSpeech/africa-g2p) (English: espeak-ng); the package does the conversion.
- Formats: `model.safetensors` (PyTorch, fp32), `gguf/africa-tts-q8_0.gguf` (audio.cpp, the default CPU engine) and an int8 [sherpa-onnx](https://github.com/k2-fsa/sherpa-onnx) bundle for phones ([sherpa-onnx/](https://huggingface.co/AfriSpeech/africa-tts/tree/main/sherpa-onnx)).

# drvexo-4b-unified **图文理解 · 语音交流 · 自定义声音 · 候选决策** 驭介智能 · Yujie Intelligence **简体中文** | [English](README_EN.md) [Hugging Face 模型](https://huggingface.co/DRVEXO-LLM/drvexo-4b-unified) · [ModelScope 模型](https://modelscope.cn/models/DRVEXOLLM/drvexo-4b-unified) [Hugging Face Space](https://huggingface.co/spaces/DRVEXO-LLM/drvexo-4b-demo) · [ModelScope 创空间](https://modelscope.cn/studios/DRVEXOLLM/drvexo-4b-demo) · [评测结果](#evaluations) · [模型亮点](#highlights) · [效果展示](#examples) · [快速开始](#quickstart) · [HTTP API](#http-api) · [许可](#license)
drvexo-4b-unified 是驭介智能开发的多模态交互模型，采用 **4B 语言主干**，将视觉理解、听觉输入、文字对话、语音生成和候选决策整合到一个可独立加载的完整模型包中。面向语音通信、智能外呼、语音控制与具身应用，提供本地 Python 与 vLLM-Omni 服务入口。 ## 评测结果 ![DRVEXO 能力表现：指令遵循、数学推理、知识理解、视觉理解、图表理解、决策能力](media/public-benchmarks-single-radar-zh-20261107.png)
评测口径 能力轴分别对应 IFEval（严格题级，541 题）、MATH-500（500 题）、MMLU-Pro（按学科比例分层抽样的 3,000 题子集，2338/3000，77.93%）、MMMU（900 题 validation）、ChartQA（1,920 题 validation）和 JevBench（231 题公开子集）。知识理解采用长思考设置；77.93% 是子集实测结果，不代表 MMLU-Pro 全量成绩。各轴展示对应任务的实测分数。
### 吞吐与语音延迟 2026 年 11 月 7 日，NVIDIA DGX Spark / GB10 上的完整模型服务实测： | 文本并发 | 总输出吞吐（token/s） | 首段文字中位数 | | ---: | ---: | ---: | | 1 | 24.02 | 58 ms | | 8 | 185.17 | 143 ms | | 32 | 601.55 | 361 ms | | 128 | **1,378.94** | 806 ms | 固定 37 个输入 token、每请求 256 个输出 token，关闭思考与前缀缓存，按整批输出和完整耗时计算。128 档 128/128 请求结束；所有档共 171 请求，测试期间错误与抢占均为 0。这是固定长度文本负载的总吞吐。 另测 3 次语音流，首个音频块 **307–324 ms**，生成速度 **2.45–2.58 倍实时**，输出采样率 24 kHz。语音结果为独立流式测试，不代表 128 路并发语音或物理播放延迟。 ## 模型亮点 - **视觉与语言交互**：支持图片问答、场景描述与可见信息提取，通过已提交的完整对话历史承接追问。 - **中英文语音交流**：支持音频输入、语音转写、文字回答与语音生成；流式文字和分块音频便于边接收边播放。 - **参考录音自定义声音**：使用已获授权的参考录音，为新的内容生成对应音色的语音，无需为每位说话人重新训练。 - **内置候选决策**：根据显式任务、背景和候选项直接评分，为客服跟进、语音控制和交互应用提供选择依据；实际执行由应用负责。 - **Tool call 与结构化输出**：生成工具调用，根据工具结果继续回答，并通过 JSON Schema 提取业务字段。 - **完整模型、统一入口**：视觉、听觉、语言、语音生成、声音参考与决策资源统一打包，支持独立加载和服务部署。 ### 在线体验 [Hugging Face Space](https://huggingface.co/spaces/DRVEXO-LLM/drvexo-4b-demo)　|　[ModelScope 创空间](https://modelscope.cn/studios/DRVEXOLLM/drvexo-4b-demo) 提供文字与图片对话、麦克风和摄像头输入、流式朗读、参考声音、候选评分，以及可编辑的系统提示词。演示共享自托管服务，繁忙时按队列处理。仅提交非敏感内容和已获授权的录音。 通话信令、拨号、电话线路、音频播放和实际工具或设备执行由应用层提供。 ## 效果展示 ### 图片理解 · 宇航员照片 **用户：** 请具体描述这张照片中人物的服装、装备、姿态，以及背景中可见的物体。只依据画面，不要猜测人物姓名、拍摄日期或正在执行的任务。 **模型实际回答节选：** > 人物穿着一件橙红色的宇航服，材质看似为光滑的合成纤维。 > > 前景右下角放置一个黑色头盔，表面光滑反光，顶部有白色条纹，侧面可见银色固定装置。 > > 人物正对镜头，头部略微前倾，面带微笑，表情自然。 > > 左侧为一面美国国旗，星条旗清晰可见，悬挂于背景中。 > > 右侧背景中有一枚航天器模型，主体为白色，带有棕色助推器，外形类似航天飞机。 图片来源：NASA，公有领域，由 scikit-image 分发。以上为原始输出节选；完整回答中的徽章文字、头盔佩戴和手套细节存在误读。 ### Tool call · 订单与双仓库存查询 ![三次只读工具调用的真实记录回放](media/tool-replay-zh-20261107.gif) **用户：** 查询演示订单 EX-20261107-01 的状态，同时比较杭州仓和上海仓 EXO-17 的可用库存。只做查询，不修改订单、不调货。 模型生成 **3 次工具调用**：查询订单状态，以及杭州、上海两仓库存。应用返回演示数据后，模型回答订单已出库、杭州仓可用库存 **18**、上海仓 **7**。使用本地合成业务数据，未连接真实订单系统或修改订单。 [打开交互式回放](media/interactive-showcase-20261107.html?demo=tool&lang=zh) · 支持暂停、重播与逐步查看，播放节奏不代表推理时延。 ### JSON Schema · 嵌套订单字段提取 **用户：** 客户林舟订购 EXO-17 两件、EXO-23 一件，送到杭州，希望明天下午14:00–16:00送达。 按照预先提交的对象与数组 Schema，模型实际输出： ```json { "customer": "林舟", "items": [ {"sku": "EXO-17", "quantity": 2}, {"sku": "EXO-23", "quantity": 1} ], "delivery": {"city": "杭州", "time_window": "14:00–16:00"} } ``` 输出通过本例 Schema 校验；时间字段保留时段，未解析“明天”的日期。 ### Decision · 时间、偏好与授权边界 ![四候选客服跟进方案评分的真实记录回放](media/decision-replay-zh-20261107.gif) **背景：** 客户今天 18:00 后才方便接听电话，现在希望先收到邮件摘要；未授权下单或修改地址。 在四个候选方案中，模型选择 **“现在发送邮件摘要，18:00 后再按约电话跟进，不修改订单”**，候选概率 **99.42%**。其余候选分别为立即催促接听、擅自下单、擅自改地址。响应 `executable: false`，没有实际发送邮件、拨打电话或操作设备。 [打开交互式回放](media/interactive-showcase-20261107.html?demo=decision&lang=zh) · 候选概率不代表执行成功率。 ### 默认声音 · 简短问候 你好，很高兴和你聊天。 [播放 / 下载](media/greeting.wav) ### 默认声音 · 西湖介绍 杭州西湖是中国著名的淡水湖泊，也是世界文化遗产和国家级风景名胜区。它以其“湖光山色”的绝美景色闻名，拥有苏堤春晓、断桥残雪等十处经典景观。每年吸引数百万游客前来欣赏其四季不同的自然风光与深厚的历史文化底蕴。 [播放 / 下载](media/west-lake.wav) 以上音频为历史参考基线的实际默认音色样例；当前服务的自定义声音可在 Space 中上传授权录音体验。 ## 快速开始 ### 下载模型 从 [Hugging Face](https://huggingface.co/DRVEXO-LLM/drvexo-4b-unified) 或 [ModelScope](https://modelscope.cn/models/DRVEXOLLM/drvexo-4b-unified) 下载完整模型包，任选一种方式： ```bash # Hugging Face python -m pip install -U huggingface_hub hf download DRVEXO-LLM/drvexo-4b-unified --local-dir ./drvexo-4b-unified # ModelScope python -m pip install -U modelscope modelscope download DRVEXOLLM/drvexo-4b-unified --local-dir ./drvexo-4b-unified ``` ### 本地运行 准备 Linux / CUDA 环境与完整模型目录，先安装匹配 CUDA 的 PyTorch、torchaudio，再安装包内依赖： ```bash cd /path/to/drvexo-4b-unified python -m pip install -r requirements.txt # 文本对话 python example.py chat --text "请介绍一下你自己。" # 图片问答 python example.py chat --text "提取图中的时间、项目名称和数量。" --image image.jpg # 语音转写 python example.py asr --audio input.wav # 参考音频自定义声音 python example.py voice --text "你好，很高兴和你交流。" \ --reference reference.wav --output output.wav ``` 参考录音建议使用已获授权的 1–30 秒单声道语音。命令行聊天默认最多生成 128 个新 token；长回答可用 Python 显式设置预算： ```python from pathlib import Path from PIL import Image from drvexo_unified import UnifiedModel model = UnifiedModel(Path("."), device="cuda") print(model.chat("请介绍一下你自己。", max_new_tokens=256)["text"]) image = Image.open("image.jpg").convert("RGB") print(model.chat("请描述图片中的内容。", image=image, max_new_tokens=512)["text"]) ``` ### 启动 vLLM-Omni 服务 使用 **vLLM 0.33 与包含 DRVEXO 适配的源码**。先按目标平台准备匹配的 CUDA、PyTorch、vLLM 与源码依赖，再安装下列固定修订： ```bash git clone --branch codex/drvexo-speech-general-20261030 \ https://github.com/DRVEXO-LLM/vllm-omni.git drvexo-vllm-omni cd drvexo-vllm-omni git checkout 6d9c034aa37c0bdf6c2bbc5d4124ddb9c6630e83 python -m pip install --no-deps -e . vllm serve /path/to/drvexo-4b-unified --omni \ --deploy-config vllm_omni/deploy/drvexo_unified.yaml \ --served-model-name drvexo-4b-unified \ --host 127.0.0.1 --port 8091 \ --enable-auto-tool-choice --tool-call-parser qwen3_xml ``` 适配入口见 [PR #9645](https://github.com/vllm-project/vllm-omni/pull/9645)，请使用上述固定源码；不要默认标准发行版已经包含此适配。面向外网提供服务时，请配置认证与访问控制。 ## HTTP API OpenAI 兼容的文字 SSE 示例： ```bash curl -N http://127.0.0.1:8091/v1/chat/completions \ -H 'Content-Type: application/json' \ -d '{"model":"drvexo-4b-unified","messages":[{"role":"user","content":"你好，请介绍一下自己。"}],"modalities":["text"],"max_tokens":256,"stream":true}' ``` 文字与默认声音的分句语音一起流式返回： ```bash curl -N http://127.0.0.1:8091/v1/drvexo/chat/stream \ -H 'Content-Type: application/json' \ -d '{"request":{"model":"drvexo-4b-unified","messages":[{"role":"user","content":"请简单介绍西湖。"}],"max_tokens":256},"audio_output":true,"speech_language":"Chinese"}' ``` | 接口 | 用途 | | --- | --- | | `POST /v1/chat/completions` | 文本、多轮、图片、语音输入；JSON Schema、工具调用 | | `POST /v1/audio/speech` | 参考声音合成：`input`、`task_type:"Base"`、`ref_audio`、`x_vector_only_mode:true`、`response_format:"wav"` | | `POST /v1/drvexo/speech` | 默认声音朗读：`text`、`language`；返回 WAV | | `POST /v1/drvexo/speech/stream` | 指定文本分块语音 | | `POST /v1/drvexo/chat/stream` | 模型回答的文字增量与默认音色分句语音 | | `POST /v1/drvexo/decision` | 显式 `instruction`、`state`、`candidates` 与 `task` 的候选评分 | 图片使用 `image_url` 内容块，语音使用 `input_audio`；当前每次最多一图或一段音频，不支持视频。多轮历史通过 `messages` 传入。启用服务 API key 后，增加 `Authorization: Bearer `。 标准聊天流为 SSE；DRVEXO 语音流为 NDJSON，逐行处理 `text` / `audio` / `done` / `error` 事件。`audio_data` 是独立 WAV 的 base64；`text_done` 只表示文字结束，应继续等待音频与最终 `done`。客户端负责音频播放、麦克风/VAD、工具执行和设备控制；决策评分不直接执行动作。 ## # Humanness Voice Podcast

Generate a scripted podcast using two reference voices. This is the complete real-podcast full fine-tune of **Humaneness Voice Large 1.7 at update 9,874**, heard in our segment/block listening experiment. It includes the full model weights, portable inference and training code, example reference voices, and a pipeline for turning separately generated speech into longer episodes.

**[Listen: raw, trimmed and reassembled conversations](https://laion-humaneness-podcast-segment-block-pilot.static.hf.space/editing/index.html)** · **[Original measured comparison](https://laion-humaneness-podcast-segment-block-pilot.static.hf.space/index.html)** · **[Single-speaker prompting guide](guides/SINGLE_SPEAKER.md)** · **[Multi-speaker prompting guide](guides/MULTI_SPEAKER.md)** · **[Pipeline guide](guides/PIPELINE.md)** · **[Training and provenance](TRAINING.md)** · **[Agent reference](guides/AGENT_GUIDE.md)**

Model weights and newly authored LAION release materials: **CC BY 4.0**. This is a full checkpoint; no LoRA needs to be merged. The external MOSS audio codec, upstream software and reference recordings retain their own terms. See [NOTICE.md](NOTICE.md).

## What it does

You supply the dialogue, its speaker labels and emotion directions, plus one clean reference recording for each voice. The model produces speech; the surrounding pipeline checks the spoken words, trims unused audio and assembles the episode. It does not write the podcast text.

Two generation paths are included:

| Path | Generation unit | Why use it? | Main limitation |
|---|---|---|---|
| **turns** | One speaker's turn per call, with only that person's anchor | More direct control over the intended identity; easy to replace an individual turn | Separately generated turns may feel less acoustically connected |
| **pairs** | Two consecutive turns together, normally S1 then S2, with both anchors | Preserves the local interaction and one speaker change within a generation | The two identities can still merge or switch incorrectly |

Both paths can batch **different texts, prompts, speakers and candidate seeds**. Use one candidate for speed or two candidates for a small selection pool; four and eight are also supported. A run keeps every raw candidate and its acceptance/rejection record in a SQLite journal. Prefer a downloaded local model directory or pin --revision when resuming: a later repository documentation commit can otherwise resolve to a different snapshot.

The model was trained on English, German, French, Spanish and Dutch material. The current detailed reference/segment comparison covers **English and German**, using the same listener-approved German voices for both. Do not assume equally established quality in all five languages.

## Quick start

Use a CUDA-capable machine. The recorded software stack is Python 3.13.5, PyTorch 2.9.1 and Transformers 5.14.1; install matching CUDA Torch and torchaudio 2.9.1 builds appropriate for your machine first. The new portable driver has CPU contract tests; consult [VALIDATION.md](VALIDATION.md) for the exact GPU test status and known limits.

The quick-start commands below enable **unvalidated automatic quiet-pause trimming** as an experiment. Omit --compact-pauses to retain internal timing.

~~~bash
hf download laion/Humanness-Voice-Podcast --local-dir humanness-podcast
cd humanness-podcast
python -m pip install -r requirements.txt

# One referenced speaker per generation; two seeded candidates per turn.
python infer.py --model . \
  --script examples/short_en.json --output runs/en-turns \
  --mode turns --candidates 2 --batch-size 2 --compact-pauses

# Generate two turns at once, then assemble the chosen blocks.
python infer.py --model . \
  --script examples/episode_de.json --output runs/de-pairs \
  --mode pairs --candidates 2 --batch-size 2 --compact-pauses
~~~

Open runs/en-turns/listening.html or runs/de-pairs/listening.html. It updates as candidates and selected units appear. The completed episode is episode.wav; episode_timeline.json records the assembly clock.

The script examples use the same two German voices as the listening experiment. [Four short input references and exact cached MOSS anchor codes](examples/references/) are included: a German pair and the earlier English pair. The English and German example scripts deliberately share the German anchors. Edit their references and reference_codes fields to use the English pair, or remove reference_codes when supplying new audio. Use clean, single-speaker references of approximately **5–15 seconds**; the codec limit is 63–187 frames, or 5.04–14.96 seconds. The old three-second truncation is not used.

The speech decoder uses the separately downloaded [MOSS Audio Tokenizer v2](https://huggingface.co/OpenMOSS-Team/MOSS-Audio-Tokenizer-v2). The package downloads it when needed. Pass --codec /local/codec to reuse an existing copy. The repository is self-contained for the TTS weights and code; codec and optional scoring/conversion dependencies are separate downloads.

## Automatic trimming and episode assembly

The default speech cut keeps up to **80 ms before the first verified script word and 150 ms after the last**. Gentle fades of up to 20 ms at the start and 50 ms at the end stay outside those words. The first/last **requested script words** define the cut, rather than any later ASR words from mumbling.

Selected units are assembled from lossless 48-kHz masters and encoded/written as one episode. The default **400-ms word-to-word gap** includes retained tail/head padding. It does not add another 400 ms on top of those guards.

**Additional long-pause trimming is experimental and UNVALIDATED.** Enable it explicitly:

~~~bash
python infer.py --model . \
  --script examples/episode_en.json --output runs/en-quiet-trim \
  --mode turns --candidates 2 --batch-size 2 \
  --tail-ms 150 --compact-pauses --pause-trigger 0.8 --pause-keep 0.18
~~~

This option tests gaps between recognized words, preserves the words themselves, and shortens only long gaps that are quiet under both an absolute and a relative RMS threshold. Eligible pauses become approximately **180 ms**, with a 10-ms constant-gain crossfade to avoid a background-level bump. It can still remove faint speech or intentional nonverbal sounds that ASR misses. It has signal-level tests but no listening validation. Keep it off when preserving those details is more important than shortening pauses.

The listening grid demonstrates the earlier script-boundary editing workflow, **not this new internal-pause compaction**. Its diagnostic examples compare 100/150/200-ms tails. Source quality and WER values are not copied onto newly edited outputs.

## Candidate selection and content checks

These rewards select fixed-model candidates; the episode CLI does not update model weights. The default reward is:

~~~text
R = (0.5 × C + 0.5 × M) / (1 + WER)

C: speaker-balanced mean cosine to the intended EARS identity embedding.
M: positive own-reference versus other-reference contrast, normalized by
   max(1 - reference_cross_cosine, 0.05), then clipped to [0,1].
~~~

Missing/scant aligned speech contributes zero to identity ranking. Speaker labels are never swapped to improve the score. The inverse-WER factor is bounded at zero WER.

Before ranking, candidates must have verified script endpoints, sufficient literal-word coverage for every intended turn, and WER below the configured threshold inside the kept script span. Extra post-script material is removed; hallucinated words **inside** the kept span still count as errors. If no candidate passes, the pipeline stops with its journal and listening page intact. It does not silently publish an incomplete episode or loosen QA.

--reward pleasant adds a **proposed, unvalidated** pleasantness preference:

~~~text
R = (0.4 × C + 0.2 × M + 0.2 × Genuine_CDF + 0.2 × CE_CDF) / (1 + WER)
~~~

Genuine and actual Audiobox CE use the fixed EARS training-distribution Gaussian-CDF normalization. --reward asr skips identity scoring and ranks by 1/(1+WER); it is a faster content-only option, not an identity check.

The default judge is [Humaneness EARS Medium](https://huggingface.co/laion/humaneness-ears-base-medium). Identity ranking uses its 250-dimensional identity embedding; the separate 128-dimensional timbre embedding should not be confused with it.

## ASR: exact implementation

The verified default is **[Parakeet Redux](https://huggingface.co/moondream/parakeet-redux)** through Photon, with actual word timestamps. Its timestamps are already global; the code does not add segment offsets twice.

An official multilingual “Parakeet V4” checkpoint could not be verified when this package was prepared. We do not invent a model ID or call Redux “V4.” Use --asr-model for a compatible Photon model or --asr-command asr_command.json for a separately installed ASR service. The command receives JSON on stdin and must return text plus globally timestamped words under segments[].words[]. See [the pipeline guide](guides/PIPELINE.md). --asr-model-path supports an already downloaded Photon checkpoint.

## Optional identity conversion

The [Humaneness Voice Converter](https://huggingface.co/laion/Humaneness-Voice-Converter) can be used as an **experimental optional post-processing stage**:

~~~bash
# Install the converter separately, following its own README.
hf download laion/Humaneness-Voice-Converter --local-dir ../humaneness-vc

python infer.py --model . \
  --script examples/short_en.json --output runs/en-pairs-vc \
  --mode pairs --candidates 2 --batch-size 2 \
  --vc-model-dir ../humaneness-vc \
  --vc-python /path/to/converter-venv/bin/python \
  --vc-buffer-ms 100 --tail-ms 150
~~~

For a paired block, ASR locates each intended turn. Up to 100 ms of source buffer is kept on either side, limited by the midpoint to neighboring turns. Each speaker is converted separately to **their own** reference. Converted speech is resampled, transcribed again, checked against its intended text, trimmed and reassembled in chronological order. Source turns must fit the converter's tested 1–30-second range. An unsafe split or failed post-conversion check stops the run.

Conversion can change duration and expression; this route does not pretend that converted audio can always be pasted back at the old sample offsets. It rebuilds the timeline with controlled word-clock gaps and edge fades. It has not been validated end to end as a podcast production workflow and does not guarantee correct identity.

## Training, architecture and reproducibility

This is a full supervised fine-tune of [Humaneness Voice Large 1.7](https://huggingface.co/laion/Humaneness-Voice-Large-1.7). The MOSS Local Transformer architecture uses a Qwen-family semantic backbone and a local acoustic transformer to generate twelve codec channels per 80-ms frame. The external MOSS-v2 decoder renders 48-kHz mono speech.

Training used two epochs, approximately 80% real-podcast / 20% original-format acting replay by presentation count, 32 GPUs and 9,874 optimizer updates. Peak learning rates were 2e-5 for the semantic backbone and 4e-5 for the local/acoustic parameters; 5% warm-up followed by cosine decay to 10% of the peak. The final measured development loss was **4.4653**, versus **4.5745** before training. This alone is not a human listening-quality result.

See [TRAINING.md](TRAINING.md) for the actual counts, data contract, original frozen launch archive, portable continued-SFT entry point and checkpoint/resume instructions. This repository contains deployment weights, not the 32-rank historical optimizer state. Starting a new fine-tune from these BF16 weights is not an exact optimizer resume of the completed training run.

## Known limitations and intended use

Speaker identities can collapse, switches can be late, and generation can continue into silence or mumbling. Duration requests are approximate, not millisecond-accuracy guarantees. ASR-based checks and automatic identity/quality scores can be wrong. Batched generation changes floating-point arithmetic; fixed seeds do not promise bit-identical results across hardware, precision or batch size.
